name: Lies, Lies, Lies

items.name: The Hula Burger (McDonald's)
items.fact: In 1963 McDonald's tested a “burger” with a grilled slice of pineapple instead of meat, for Catholic customers who ate no meat on Fridays. The Filet-O-Fish beat it and stayed on the menu.

items.name: Bubblegum broccoli (McDonald's)
items.fact: McDonald's once developed broccoli that tasted of bubblegum, hoping children would eat more vegetables. In 2014 its boss admitted the test had failed: the children were simply confused by the taste.

items.name: Chocolate fries (McDonald's Japan)
items.fact: In 2016 McDonald's in Japan sold the McChoco Potato for a limited time: a normal portion of salty French fries with chocolate sauce poured all over them.

items.name: Rice burger (MOS Burger)
items.fact: The Japanese chain MOS Burger sells burgers without a bread bun. Instead, the filling, such as beef in a sweet and salty sauce, goes between two flat, grilled cakes of pressed rice.

items.name: Spaghetti with hot dogs (Jollibee)
items.fact: Jollibee, the biggest fast-food chain in the Philippines, serves spaghetti in a sweet tomato sauce with sliced hot dogs and grated cheese. Part of the sweetness comes from banana ketchup.

items.name: Deer sandwich (Arby's)
items.fact: In 2016 the American chain Arby's sold a venison (deer meat) steak sandwich for a few days in states where many people hunt. In some restaurants it sold out within minutes.

items.name: Pickle-juice slush (Sonic)
items.fact: In summer 2018 the American drive-in chain Sonic sold a bright green frozen slush drink flavoured with pickle juice: the salty, sour liquid from jars of pickled gherkins.

items.name: Foie gras burger (Wendy's Japan)
items.fact: When Wendy's came back to Japan in 2011, it sold a luxury burger topped with foie gras, the expensive French duck or goose liver, for about $16, several times the price of a normal burger.

items.name: Unicorn Frappuccino (Starbucks)
items.fact: In 2017 Starbucks sold a pink and blue iced drink that changed colour and flavour as you stirred it, from sweet and fruity to sour. It was on sale for only a few days.

items.name: The upside-down Blizzard (Dairy Queen)
items.fact: Dairy Queen staff traditionally hand over its thick Blizzard ice-cream dessert upside down, to show how thick it is. The chain has even promised a free one if it falls out of the cup.

fakes.name: Porridge burger
fakes.fact: A Glasgow fast-food chain sold a “porridge burger” for one winter: a beef burger between two fried oatcake buns, with a small pot of whisky-flavoured sauce for dipping.

fakes.name: Cola-boiled chips
fakes.fact: A Belgian chip-shop chain boils its chips in cola before frying them, so they come out dark brown and slightly sweet. It sells them in a paper cone with mayonnaise.

fakes.name: Matcha ketchup
fakes.fact: A Japanese burger chain sells bright green ketchup made with matcha green tea as a spring-only sauce for its fries. It tastes like normal ketchup, but a little bitter.

fakes.name: Fish-finger milkshake
fakes.fact: A British seaside burger chain sold a vanilla milkshake with crushed fish fingers blended in, for one week in August, as a joke for its 50th birthday. Around 3,000 were sold.

fakes.name: Sauerkraut soft-serve
fakes.fact: An Austrian burger chain sells a soft ice cream swirled with sweetened sauerkraut and apple every autumn. It comes in a cone made from pretzel dough, and staff say it sells best to students.

fakes.name: Tomato-soup slush
fakes.fact: A Dutch fast-food chain sells a frozen tomato-soup slush with basil every summer. It comes with a small cheese toastie for dipping, and it is served with a spoon instead of a straw.

fakes.name: Ketchup ice lolly
fakes.fact: A Danish hot-dog chain sells an ice lolly made of frozen, sweetened ketchup and mustard in two stripes, to eat after a hot dog on hot days.

fakes.name: Beetroot-soup milkshake
fakes.fact: A Lithuanian fast-food chain sells a bright pink milkshake made from cold beetroot soup and vanilla ice cream every summer. Staff say tourists order it for the colour, then rarely finish it.

fakes.name: Mushy-pea fizzy drink
fakes.fact: A British fish-and-chip chain sells a green fizzy drink flavoured with mushy peas and mint. It is only on sale at its seaside restaurants, in summer.

fakes.name: Rice-pudding pizza
fakes.fact: A Swedish pizza chain sells a dessert pizza topped with cold rice pudding, cinnamon and orange slices every December. It comes on a normal pizza base, cut into eight slices.

tips: Be specific: numbers, dates and real places make a lie believable.
Give it a small problem (“it went soggy in ten minutes”): perfect things sound fake.
